mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same quarter predicts a contractionary demand shock that depresses corporate earnings and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one NBER-defined recession window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that elevates wage inflation and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not trigger during a period of confirmed wage acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a NBER manufacturing recession.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% and an increase in the federal funds rate above 4% within the same month signals a dual inflationary and restrictive policy shock that increases uncertainty and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 103 AND FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period with both CPI > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.4%) combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% signals a robust demand expansion that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.4% AND HOUST monthly change > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of confirmed GDP acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for five consecutive months signals an overheating labor market that precedes a policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a subsequent FEDFUNDS hike cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion that lifts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.4% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of confirmed industrial rebound.
